campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered renewing an interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, along with two public hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar and for Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application through the public works department and approving new consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization to submit a grant application through the Public Works Director
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — March 18, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council held a public hearing on a proposed ordinance and then formally introduced it, taking the first procedural step required before it can become law. The Council waived a full reading of the ordinance's text and directed staff to bring it back for final adoption on the consent calendar at the next regular meeting.
keyTopics: Public hearing on a proposed city ordinance
First reading and introduction of the ordinance
Waiver of full text reading of the ordinance
Scheduling final adoption for the next regular meeting's consent calendar

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — May 19, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council considered routine business including approval of prior closed session minutes and the March 2026 financial and investment report. The Council also considered several service and construction agreements, including a paving contract with O'Grady Paving, a housing-related agreement with HouseKeys, and grant applications and a project list tied to state transportation funding.
keyTopics: March 2026 monthly financial and investment report
Construction contract with O'Grady Paving
Five-year agreement with HouseKeys
Grant applications for a statewide funding program
Resolution adopting a list of state-funded projects for fiscal year 2026-27

san-jose.title: San José City Council — August 11, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council met to handle routine administrative business, including approving prior council and committee meeting minutes and making appointments to various city committees, boards, and commissions. The Council also considered general authorization for grants related to the airport and a proposed amendment to the city's employee deferred compensation plan.
keyTopics: Approval of City Council and Council Committee meeting minutes
Council appointments to committees, boards, and commissions
General authorization for airport grants
Amendment to the City of San José Deferred Compensation Plan

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — August 17, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to hear public comments, discuss plans for the city's Summer Movie Nights event, and review the committee's overall role before electing members to leadership positions like chair and vice chair. Members also gave updates on their individual committee work and looked ahead to upcoming meetings of other city boards and commissions.
keyTopics: Public comments from residents
Planning for Summer Movie Nights
Overview of the Youth Advisory Committee's purpose and responsibilities
Election of committee leadership roles (chair/vice chair)
Updates on other city boards, commissions, and committees

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 11, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: Sunnyvale's City Council held a special study session to discuss raising requirements for affordable housing in new developments and updating the fees developers can pay instead of building those affordable units. The regular 7 P.M. council meeting followed, opening with the flag salute.
keyTopics: Proposed increases to inclusionary housing requirements for new rental and ownership projects
Updates to below market rate (BMR) in-lieu fees paid by developers
Review of Council Priority Project CDD 23-01 on affordable housing policy
Impact of housing policy changes on new residential construction

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission met to plan the upcoming Bike Fest event and reviewed the Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program. Commissioners also heard from a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI and approved the minutes from their June 10, 2026 meeting. Time was set aside for members of the public to speak on any topic not already on the agenda.
keyTopics: Planning for the Bike Fest event
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program review
Presentation from youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes
Open public comment period

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — July 14, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council considered an agreement between the City and Santa Clara County to fund and operate a 30-unit interim housing project on county-owned land at Lawrence Expressway and Benton Street. Under the deal, the City would provide limited funding to help run the Homekey-funded housing development, which is intended to give families a temporary place to live.
keyTopics: City-County agreement to fund and operate the Santa Clara Family Community Interim Housing Project
30-unit Homekey interim housing development at Lawrence Expressway and Benton Street
City's role in providing limited operational funding rather than building costs
Use of county-owned land for temporary family housing

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on the ballot, which would replace the current business license tax with a tiered gross receipts tax. The proposal was framed as a way to make business taxes fairer, protect small businesses (about 85% of which would see minimal impact), and keep Milpitas competitive with other cities while simplifying tax administration.
keyTopics: Resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on the ballot
Shift from flat business license tax to a tiered gross receipts tax
Protections for small businesses with lower annual gross receipts
Comparing Milpitas's tax revenue and competitiveness to other cities
Simplifying tax administration and adapting to new types of businesses, including tech and gig-economy models

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — August 6, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council considered proposed process and design standards for larger wireless communication equipment (Tier 2 and Tier 3 facilities) installed on poles and other structures in city streets and sidewalks. Staff presented recommendations aimed at guiding how these installations are reviewed, approved, and designed so they fit in with the surrounding streetscape. The item was classified as not requiring environmental review under state law (CEQA).
keyTopics: Design standards for wireless equipment in the public right-of-way
Differences between Tier 2 and Tier 3 wireless facility classifications
Review and approval process for new wireless installations
Staff presentation and recommendations to the Council
CEQA exemption status for the proposed standards
